title: Adaptive Horizon Coalescer to Reduce KV Churn for Interleaved Short/Long Dialogs
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed-turn traffic (short prompts with short responses interleaved with long prompts that produce long responses) causes frequent KV cache churn and GPU memory fragmentation. The continuous batcher often coalesces heterogeneous requests into slots that lead to early eviction of large long-turn KV entries or excessive fragmentation from speculative reservations. This increases tail latency for long-turns and raises per-token GPU memory overhead.

Hypothesis: Introducing an adaptive horizon-aware coalescer in the continuous batching scheduler that maintains per-cohort horizon estimates and uses soft reservations for long-turn KV residency will reduce KV eviction rate and defragment GPU slabs, improving p50/p99 latency for long-turns without materially harming short-turn latency or throughput.

Proposed approach: Implement a scheduler component (horizon coalescer) that: (1) tracks running and historical sequence-length distributions per route/cohort, (2) computes a dynamic coalescing window (horizon) and a token-reservation budget per slot, (3) prefers grouping requests with compatible horizons and reorders admission within latency SLO bounds, (4) uses soft KV reservations that pin prefix KV for a small time budget to avoid eviction during anticipated multi-step long-turns, and (5) extends eviction scoring to factor in predicted continuation probability and slab fragmentation cost.

Trade-offs and risks: Additional CPU and metadata memory for tracking histograms and reservation bookkeeping. Potentially higher short-turn admission latency if coalescer waits to coalesce compatible requests; mitigation via latency budget gates and emergency fast-path. Complexity in correctness across private/dedicated deployment variants (clock skew, observability differences).

Goals: Reduce KV eviction rate for long-turn flows by >=30%, reduce GPU slab fragmentation metric by >=20%, keep 95th percentile latency regression for short-turns <5% and p99 for long-turns improved by >=15% on benchmarked mixlen traffic.
acceptance_criteria: KV eviction rate for long-turn cohort reduced by at least 30% on mixlen benchmark (compared to baseline runtime-1.21).
GPU slab fragmentation index reduced by at least 20% under sustained mixlen traffic (48h soak).
End-to-end p99 latency for long-turns improves by >=15% relative to baseline while short-turn p95 degrades <5%.
Feature gated behind runtime toggle and can be fully disabled without config reload.
Unit and integration tests for horizon calculations, reservation bookkeeping, and eviction scoring added to CI with deterministic seeds.
measurements: Baseline test: 70% short-turns (<=32 tokens), 30% long-turns (>=512 tokens) over 1M requests; measure KV evictions, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU memory RSS, slab fragmentation metric.
Target: KV evictions_long_turn_cohort <= 70% of baseline, slab_fragmentation_index <= 80% of baseline.
Latency targets: short_turn_p95 <= 105% of baseline, long_turn_p99 <= 85% of baseline.
Throughput: no more than 5% drop in sustained throughput at target concurrency for dedicated nodes.
experiment_plan: Design doc + sequence diagrams (link below) to be reviewed by runtime and infra owners.
Prototype in scheduler-experiments branch: horizon estimator (exponential decay histogram), soft reservation store, coalescer admission policy.
Microbench: run synthetic mixlen microbench on single-GPU instance to validate logic and measure CPU overhead.
Scale test: run 48h soak on a 4x A100 pool using mixlen traffic generator; collect evictions, fragmentation, latency histograms.
Iterate thresholds (reservation time budget, horizon smoothing alpha, admission latency gate) based on results.
Code review, perf signoff, and staged rollout.
rollout_plan: Canary: enable on 1% of hosted traffic in us-west for 24h with extended logging and eviction traces.
Ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over several days only if metrics meet success criteria.
Dedicated: offer as an opt-in config for dedicated pools for initial customers, validated by internal benchmarks.
Rollback: immediate toggle off if p99 latency for any cohort regresses >10% or CPU overhead >20% vs baseline.
notes: Related ticket: ENG-314159 (continuous-batcher-length-drift-mitigation) - dependency for shared histograms
updates: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: Design doc drafted; reviewed with serving-runtime and kv-cache owners. Decided on exponential moving histogram with 1k-bin compression to limit metadata size.

2026-03-04 - Prototype: Horizon estimator and soft-reservation store implemented (scheduler-experiments branch). Early microbench shows ~7% CPU overhead on scheduler thread for 1k concurrent slots; acceptable but will optimize allocations.
2026-03-06 - Eviction scoring: added continuation-probability term; initial offline simulation on historical request traces reduces eviction of long-turn KV by ~28% in trace replay.

2026-03-08 - Integration test: added deterministic unit tests for horizon smoothing and reservation expiry; flaky test found in high-concurrency path and fixed (race condition in reservation cleanup).
2026-03-10 - Scale run scheduled for 2026-03-12: 48h soak on 4x A100; telemetry + deep traces instrumented. Preparing canary rollback runbook.
